key_insight: Rust’s ownership model, translated through Aeneas into Lean, enables scalable machine-checked verification of production cryptographic code without low-level aliasing and liveness reasoning.
engineering_relevance: The approach shows that verified Rust can remain performant, portable, and maintainable enough for real cryptographic systems like Microsoft’s SymCrypt across x86-64 and ARM.
method: Extract Rust code into a pure Lean model with Aeneas
Use Lean tactics and libraries to prove safety, panic-freedom, and functional correctness
Leverage AI agents for proof writing and for formalizing standards and intrinsics under expert review
evidence_signal: The authors report a 237 KLOC Lean development verifying 16.7 KLOC of Rust code for post-quantum cipher suites, including SHA-3 and ML-KEM implementations.
watch_item: Formalizing cryptographic standards and platform-specific intrinsics still requires expert design and review, so full automation is not yet achieved.
paper_title: Scaling Verification of Cryptographic Software with Aeneas, Rust, and Lean
